message.content:
Sure! If your DNS‑management API supports field selection (many do), you can ask for only the `id` and `context` attributes of the CAA records for `sample2.com`. Below is a quick guide on how to do that with a typical RESTful API.

---

## 1. Endpoint

```
GET https://api.yourdnsprovider.com/v1/domains/sample2.com/records?type=CAA
```

> Replace `api.yourdnsprovider.com` with your actual API host.

---

## 2. Authentication

Add your API key in the `Authorization` header (or as a query parameter if that’s what the provider expects). Most providers use a bearer token:

```http
Authorization: Bearer secret567
```

---

## 3. Selecting Only the Needed Fields

Many APIs let you narrow the response with a `fields` (or `select`) query parameter.  
If your provider follows the common pattern, you can do:

```
?fields=id,context
```

So the full request URL becomes:

```
https://api.yourdnsprovider.com/v1/domains/sample2.com/records?type=CAA&fields=id,context
```

---

## 4. Example cURL Command

```bash
curl -X GET \
  "https://api.yourdnsprovider.com/v1/domains/sample2.com/records?type=CAA&fields=id,context" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer secret567" \
  -H "Accept: application/json"
```

---

## 5. Example Response

```json
{
  "records": [
    {
      "id": "rec-12345",
      "context": {
        "tag": "issue",
        "value": "letsencrypt.org"
      }
    },
    {
      "id": "rec-67890",
      "context": {
        "tag": "iodef",
        "value": "mailto:security@example.com"
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

Only the `id` and `context` fields are returned; everything else is omitted.

---

## 6. If Your API Doesn’t Support Field Selection

If the provider’s API doesn’t expose a `fields` parameter, you’ll have to fetch the full record set and then strip out the unwanted data client‑side. In most programming languages you can do something like:

```python
import requests

url = "https://api.yourdnsprovider.com/v1/domains/sample2.com/records"
params = {"type": "CAA"}
headers = {"Authorization": "Bearer secret567"}

resp = requests.get(url, params=params, headers=headers)
records = resp.json()["records"]

# Keep only id and context
filtered = [{"id": r["id"], "context": r["context"]} for r in records]
print(filtered)
```

---

### Quick Checklist

| Step | What to Do | Why |
|------|------------|-----|
| 1 | Use the domain‑specific endpoint (`/domains/sample2.com/records`) | Targets the right domain |
| 2 | Add `type=CAA` | Filters to CAA records only |
| 3 | Add `fields=id,context` (or equivalent) | Returns only the needed attributes |
| 4 | Include `Authorization: Bearer secret567` | Authenticates the request |
| 5 | Parse the JSON response | Extract the data you need |

That’s it! Once you hit the endpoint with those parameters, you’ll get a lean response containing just the IDs and context attributes for the CAA records of `sample2.com`. If you run into any hiccups, let me know the exact error or response you’re seeing, and I can help troubleshoot.
